## Salon Booking Bot — core (Phase 2)
CP0 Echo: Webhook → Normalize (adapter boundary; sender_key = "{channel}:{id}") → Build Reply → Respond.
CP1 Front gate: Load Config (MOCK) → Validate Payload → Reject 400.
CP2 State: Load / Merge / Save State (Airtable conversations, keyed by sender_key; turn_count).
CP3 Guards: Check Bot Guards (kill-switch + max-turns) run BEFORE the LLM → Handoff Reply.
CP3 LLM intent: Build LLM Request ({today} + derived schema) → Extract Intent (HTTP → Anthropic, structured output) → Parse Intent (temp; Validate Intent + gate land in 3c).
Error branches visible (400 / 503). Zernio swaps in at Normalize (Phase 4).

## Guards — before the LLM (0 cost)
**Check Bot Guards** runs before any LLM call:
- `killSwitch` ON **or** `turn_count ≥ maxTurns` → **Handoff Reply** (200) — no LLM, no Save State (a trip is not a turn).
- else → **Save State** (`turn_count +1`) → normal flow.
Config comes from `Load Config` (`bot.killSwitch`, `bot.maxTurnsPerConversation`).

⚠️ Conscious gap (not a bug): while `stage = handoff` the bot re-sends the handoff
template on every message. The silent-lock (**Check Handoff Lock**) lands in **CP6**.

Extract Intent — ERROR output = LLM INFRA FAILURE
(timeout / 5xx / rate-limit / quota).
→ "LLM Unavailable Reply": 503 + error:"llm_unavailable",
   polite customer reply kept. DISTINCT from the
   conversational handoff (200, "Handoff Reply").
CP5: Telegram owner-alert attaches to this node.

⚠ A 5xx tells the caller to RETRY. Before Phase 4
(Zernio calls this webhook and may retry on a 503) the
status-code policy is reviewed; Phase-3 idempotency
(processed_messages) covers those repeats.
Note: all Respond nodes are the Phase-2 transport layer;
in Phase 4 the reply is sent via the Zernio send API and
this webhook response becomes an ACK (adapter boundary, node 28).
